newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece dismisses Albanian accusations of plot.
newsitem.headline: Greece dismisses Albanian accusations of plot.

text.p: Greece dismissed Albanian accusations that it was involved in the uprising in southern Albania and said on Thursday it would continue to help its Balkan neighbour to restore order.
Albania's secret police chief Bashkim Gazidede accused groups in Greece on Wednesday of plotting to "liberate" southern Albania and said this was behind the insurrection in its border region.
He told parliament that a plot called "Lotos" had been worked out by groups in Greece in 1990, when 45 years of rigid communist rule collapsed in Albania and the country was in upheaval.
"The comments by Albania's secret police chief are not even worth a denial," foreign ministry spokesman Costas Bikas said in a statement. They "must be attributed to the state of confusion he is in".
Bikas said Greece had signed a peace and friendship agreement with Albania and that "in the present crisis it helps with deeds... and works for the restoration of democratic normalcy."
Gazidede said several Greek associations were involved in the plot, and were operating out of Greece, the United States and other countries.
He named people including former Albanian army officers and Greek-Americans, who he said were involved in the "Lotos" operation.
"Lotos" was drafted in Greece and envisaged "the liberation of Northern Epirus (southern Albania) from Albanian domination through an armed insurrection", he said.

Armed rebels have seized much of south Albania this month in a popular uprising and have taken huge stocks of weapons from army munitions depots. The rebels have refused to surrender their arms until President Sali Berisha resigns.
A large ethnic Greek minority, estimated at 60,000 to 120,000 people, lives in southern Albania and has caused friction between the two Balkan neighbours in the past.
